MUQATIL:30:54-57/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r1.claim: Humans begin weak as a drop of semen, gain strength as they develop, then weaken in old age after youth and turn gray, all by God's will.

MUQATIL:30:54-57/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:54-57/r2.claim: God is all-knowing and able with respect to the Resurrection.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r2.claim: The initial weakness is the weakness of a man's semen.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r3.claim: The strength that follows this weakness is youth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p666#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid also identifies the strength following weakness as youth.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p343#2/r1.claim: Ḍaʿf in “He created you from weakness” means semen.

TAB-FULL:v18p526#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p526#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p526#2/r1.claim: God creates weakness, strength, youth, and gray hair; his knowledge encompasses creation and nothing he wills exceeds his power, including resurrecting the dead.

TAB-FULL:v18p526/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p526/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p526/r1.claim: God argues with Quraysh deniers of resurrection that he created people from a weak drop of fluid, developed their strength after childhood, then returned them to weakness and gray hair in old age.

TAB-FULL:v18p526/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p526/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p526/r2.claim: Qatada says the first weakness is semen, later weakness is senility, and grayness means white hair.

ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r3.claim: People move from weakness as embryos to strength in youth, then to weakness and gray hair after youth.

ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ZAJJAJ:v4p190#2/r4.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet corrected his reading من ضعف to ḍamma; the author prefers ḍamma on the basis of transmission.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p507/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p507/r5.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p507/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza use fatḥa on ḍād in all three occurrences of ضعف; the other readers use ḍamma, and a report gives that form to Ḥafṣ independently of ʿĀṣim.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r3.speaker: عطية عن ابن عمر
NAHHAS:v3p278/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says he recited min ḍaʿf to the Prophet, who instructed him to say min ḍuʿf; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the former and the Kufans the latter.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p278/r4.claim: The Kufan form is a verbal noun; grammarians allow the competing vocalization in words with a guttural as second or third consonant.

NAHHAS:v3p278/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p278/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p278/r5.claim: He explains the first weakness as the weakness of the human fluid stage, followed by youthful strength.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read all three occurrences with fatḥa on ḍād; the other readers use ḍamma, including Ḥafṣ in the cited report.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r2.claim: The two vocalizations are dialectal synonyms, comparable to the two forms for poverty; weakness here means creation from weak fluid.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p450/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports reciting the phrase before the Prophet, who repeated it with the ḍamma form.

SULAMI:v2p128#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p128#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p128#3/r1.claim: Human weakness means being unable to bring benefit or repel harm.

SULAMI:v2p128#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p128#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p128#3/r2.claim: The human being is weak, captive to hunger, overcome by satiety, and held by desire; only the protected are freed from it.

THALABI:v7p307/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p307/r1.claim: God creates people first from a weak drop, gives them youthful strength, then returns them to weakness and gray-haired old age.

THALABI:v7p307/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r2.speaker: يحيى وعاصم والأعمش وحمزة
THALABI:v7p307/r2.claim: They read ضعف with a fatḥa on the ḍād; the remaining readers use a ḍamma, which Abu Ubayd prefers as the Prophet's dialect.

THALABI:v7p307/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v7p307/r3.claim: He says he recited all three forms of ضعف with a ḍamma before the Prophet, who accepted his reading.

THALABI:v7p307/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r4.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
THALABI:v7p307/r4.claim: He combines both dialect forms, using the ḍamma for the first two occurrences and fatḥa for the last.

THALABI:v7p307/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r5.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v7p307/r5.claim: He assigns the ḍamma form to Quraysh and the fatḥa form to Tamim.

THALABI:v7p307/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p307/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p307/r6.claim: God creates as He wills and is all-knowing and powerful.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.claim: The initial weakness from which people are created is sperm.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.claim: The strength after early weakness is youth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.claim: Later weakness and gray hair mean old age; white hair warns of death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r4.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r4.claim: A poem calls gray hair a warning of death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p322#2/r5.claim: God creates strength and weakness as He wills, knowing His governance and powerful over His will.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says reflection on human creation should make the denier of resurrection think; Qatada and al-Kalbi identify the weak origin as a drop of fluid.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that God created people from sperm while it was in a weak state.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r3.claim: Abu Ali reads من ضعف as from something intrinsically weak, meaning fluid of little quantity, and compares 77:20.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r4.claim: The word ضعف is also read with fatḥa; the two vowels are dialectal variants, with damma preferred because the Prophet corrected Ibn Umar's fatḥa reading.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r5.claim: Childhood weakness is followed by the strength of youth, then by renewed weakness and gray hair in old age.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says old age brings weakness and senility.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r7.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p81#2/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats شيبة as a singular form with a collective sense, like قوّة and ضعف, because verbal nouns encompass kinds of states.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r1.claim: God creates every stage of weakness, strength, gray hair, and youth according to His will.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p84/r2.claim: God is all-knowing in how He manages His creation and powerful to do whatever He wills.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:54-58/r1.claim: The initial human weakness from which God creates people is the drop of semen.

JISHUMI:v8p5635/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r3.speaker: عاصم، حمزة
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r3.claim: Asim and Hamza read الضعف with fatha; other readers use damma, both dialects. Abu Ubayd prefers fatha as the Prophet's form, but Hafs differs from Asim in favor of damma on a report from Ibn Umar and the Prophet.

JISHUMI:v8p5635/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r4.speaker: عطية العوفي
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r4.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi reports that Ibn Umar read all three instances with damma and said that was how he learned them from the Prophet.

JISHUMI:v8p5635/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r5.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
JISHUMI:v8p5635/r5.claim: Asim al-Jahdari reads the first two instances with damma and the third with fatha, combining the two dialects; al-Farra says damma is Qurayshi and fatha Tamimi.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r5.claim: ضعف is read with ḍamma in Quraysh and fatḥa in Tamīm; it refers to a weak fluid, a sperm drop.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p277/r6.claim: People move from infant weakness to youthful strength, then old-age weakness and gray hair; God creates as He wills and is knowing and powerful.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r1.claim: Ḍaʿf is read with either fatḥa or ḍamma, both dialects; ḍamma is stronger because Ibn ʿUmar recited fatḥa to the Prophet and was corrected to ḍamma.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reported that when he recited “min ḍaʿf” with fatḥa, the Prophet taught him the ḍamma reading.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r3.claim: Being created “from weakness” describes the human constitution: weakness in infancy, strength from maturity to adulthood, and a return to weakness in old age.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r4.claim: Another view says the initial weakness is the drop, as in 32:8 and 77:20.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p492#2/r5.claim: Changing people through these successive conditions is a clear proof of the Creator’s knowledge and power.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r1.claim: The human life cycle is another sign showing that idols have no part in these transformations.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce weakness with ḍamma; Asim and Hamza read it with fatḥa, but Ibn Atiyya prefers the ḍamma form.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r3.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet corrected his recitation with fatḥa to the ḍamma reading; grammarians also distinguish bodily weakness by ḍamma from mental weakness by fatḥa.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن والجحدري والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r4.claim: These readers use ḍamma on the first two occurrences and fatḥa on the final one; Isa b. Umar uses two dammas.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p343/r5.claim: The first weakness is the human origin from impure fluid, strength is youth and robust vigor, and the second weakness is old age.

TABRISI:30:51-55/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:51-55/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:51-55/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim and Hamza read ḍuʿfin with ḍamma, while the other readers use fatḥa; the reading was discussed under al-Anfāl.

TABRISI:30:51-55/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:51-55/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:51-55/r8.claim: God creates people from weakness, either as drops of semen or as helpless infants, gives them youthful strength, then weakness and gray hair in old age.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r1.claim: Weakness at creation means semen, then weakness is that of childhood, strength is youth, and later weakness is old age.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p311/r2.claim: God creates whatever He wills of weakness, strength, youth, and gray age; He knows how to govern His creation and is able to do what He wills.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r1.claim: The discussion moves from cosmic signs in the winds and clouds to the human being as a sign, tracing life from weakness through strength back to weakness.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r2.claim: Initial weakness covers fetal life, birth, infancy, nursing, and weaning; strength follows in adulthood, youth, maturity, and full development.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r3.claim: After maturity come decline and old age, which is the culmination of weakness.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r4.claim: “He creates what He wills” shows that these stages are due to God's will, paralleling His spreading clouds however He wills.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r5.claim: Knowledge is foregrounded before power here because human development unfolds through stages; in the earlier resurrection passage, power was more prominent because re-creation occurs by command.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r6.claim: Knowing and power together warn and promise: God knows people's deeds and conditions, then can reward good and punish evil; knowledge precedes the acts of reward and punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p119#2/r7.claim: The phrase “best of creators” after the account of human creation joins knowledge, which makes creation excellent, with power, expressed by creating.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r1.claim: Shaybah is a verbal noun like shayb, and a verbal noun can denote a collective event; the same applies to weakness and strength.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r2.claim: The creation of what God wills includes the alternation of strength and weakness.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r3.claim: God is all-knowing in His governance and powerful to carry out His will.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r4.speaker: نحويون الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54#2/r4.claim: Kufan grammarians permit fatḥa in ḍuʿf and similarly in words with a guttural as their second or third radical.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r1.claim: This is another proof of God's power, located in the human being as a lesson for reflection.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r10.claim: A report about a man deceived in sales describes a weakness in his contract or bargaining judgment.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r2.claim: Weakness may mean the weak drop of semen from which people were created.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r3.claim: Alternatively, weakness means the infant's state of weakness and smallness at the beginning of life.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r4.claim: The strength after initial weakness is youth, followed by weakness in old age.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r5.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r5.claim: They read ḍuʿf with fatḥa in all three occurrences; the others use ḍamma, and both are Arabic variants, with ḍamma identified as the Prophet's usage.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r6.speaker: الجحدري
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r6.claim: He reads the first two occurrences with fatḥa and the last with ḍamma, combining the two dialect forms.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r7.claim: The ḍamma pronunciation belongs to Quraysh, and the fatḥa pronunciation to Tamīm.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r8.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r8.claim: Both pronunciations of weakness are opposites of strength.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:54/r9.claim: Another distinction assigns fatḥa to weakness in judgment and ḍamma to bodily weakness.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r5.claim: God begins humans in weakness, either as weak beings or from a weak origin, the sperm; later strength comes at maturity or when the spirit enters the body.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r6.claim: Old age brings weakness and gray hair; the life stages demonstrate God's power to create every state and to determine the variation in human lives.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r7.claim: Asim and Hamza pronounce the consonant ḍād in all occurrences with fatḥ; ḍamma is stronger in the author's view.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:52-54/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says he recited the phrase ضعف before the Prophet, who taught him to read it with fatḥ; both are Arabic dialects, and repetition marks different stages, not identical weakness.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r1.claim: The initial weakness is the drop of semen; strength is youth and maturity, followed by weakness and gray hair in old age.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r2.claim: God creates whichever stages He wills and knows and controls the changes; the sequence itself plainly proves an all-knowing, all-powerful Creator.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p278#3/r3.claim: The ḍād is read with fatḥa by ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, with ḍamma by the others; both are Arabic forms, but ḍamma is stronger because Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet corrected him to it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r1.claim: Human beings pass through stages from dust, sperm, embryo, and fetus to a weak newborn, then childhood, youth, strength, and finally aging, weakness, and gray hair; God acts as He wills.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p327/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar confirms to ʿAṭiyya that he recited the verse to the Prophet as ʿAṭiyya recited it to him, preserving that recitation; Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī transmit it, with al-Tirmidhī grading it ḥasan.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r4.claim: Hamza and ʿAsim, with a difference in the transmission of Hafs, read ḍaʿf with a fatḥa for weakness generally; the other readers use a ḍamma, and the author relates the weakness to the earliest developmental stages.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r5.claim: Human beings move from initial weakness through growth and full strength, then return to weakness and gray hair; the author gives approximate youth and aging milestones and explains gray hair through bodily cooling and dryness.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p641/r6.claim: These variable life stages prove God's free choice, knowledge, and power; natural causes cannot thwart what he wills, and his knowledge is named before power because knowledge entails power.

DURR-FULL:v6p501/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p501/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p501/r3.claim: When Ibn Umar recited ‘God created you from weakness,’ the Prophet prompted him to read ‘from weakness, my son’; another report says the Prophet read ḍuʿf with ḍamma, and Aisha confirms his recitation of the sequence.

DURR-FULL:v6p501/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p501/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p501/r4.claim: Qatada glosses initial weakness as a sperm drop, later weakness as old age, and gray hair as the appearance of gray.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r1.claim: The preceding Persian couplet urges people to return to their origin and seek spiritual hearing before the senses close and life's foundation collapses.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r10.claim: The inward reading warns that many who study speculative sciences to extinguish the light of the Law instead fall into the darkness of nature and seek to extinguish God's light.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r2.claim: Grammatically, الله is the subject and الذي خلقكم is its predicate; خلقكم means He brought human beings into existence.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r3.claim: The first weakness is the weak origin, semen or soil, with the verbal noun interpreted as an active noun; weakness is the opposite of strength.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r4.claim: The readings differ: fatha is Tamim's dialect and the choice of Asim and Hamza in all three places; damma is Quraysh's dialect and the choice of other readers. Ibn Umar recited fatha and the Prophet read damma.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r5.claim: The second weakness is in the fetus and child; strength first appears in movement, seeking milk, and crying to repel harm.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r6.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r6.claim: Some scholars distinguish inner strength of cognition, strength experienced in the limbs, and later ability expressed in grasping and handling.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r7.claim: After puberty comes youthful strength, then old-age weakness and gray hair; repeated indefinites indicate distinct life stages rather than the same stage repeated.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r8.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r8.claim: Al-Raghib's grammatical rule, followed by major exegetes, is that repeating an indefinite noun refers to a different instance; he applies it to two eases following one hardship.

BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p41#2/r9.claim: An inward reading makes the stages weak reason, reason strengthened by proofs, then weakened faith when desire, illusion, and imagination distort inquiry into doubts that lead one from the straight path.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r1.claim: Ishari reading: initial weakness is hesitation and confusion in seeking; strength is sincerity in seeking; later weakness is the inability to bear the weight of the confession of divine unity.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p42/r10.claim: The Prophet urged special kindness to young people, saying their hearts are tender and that youths accepted his message while elders opposed him.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r11.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p42/r11.claim: A gray hair acquired in Islam is light on Resurrection Day unless it is dyed or plucked; black dye is forbidden except for warriors, while red or yellow dye is recommended.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r12.claim: The verse implies that a person would not grow gray if God did not create gray hair in him.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r2.claim: The confession la ilaha illa Allah entails true annihilation and outward weakness from the mutual reproaches and loving exchanges of the divine lovers, which bring gray hair.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p42/r3.claim: The Prophet said that Surat Hud and its sister surahs made him gray, with Hud’s command to remain upright pointing to their loving spiritual address.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r4.claim: All the changes named in the verse, including weakness, strength, youth, and gray hair, arise by God’s will rather than by nature.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p42/r5.claim: In the fortunate, God creates strong faith and weak human nature; in the wretched, strong human nature for disbelief and weak spirituality for faith.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p42/r6.claim: God knows the fortunate and wretched and creates in them the causes of felicity and misery; He can change each person’s state.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r7.claim: Human beings should notice the changing stages of their own lives, infer the perfect Creator’s knowledge and power, and direct their faculties to obedience.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p42/r8.claim: A person should use strength in God’s obedience or, if weak, refrain from disobeying Him.

BURSEVI:v7p42/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p42/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p42/r9.claim: After sixty, bodily ailments contend with weakness for work, diminished hope, and approaching death; youth should resist laziness and repair their shortcomings.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r1.claim: The opening is a subject and predicate: God began people weak, with weakness metaphorically their foundation; min marks origin.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r10.claim: The changing stages plainly demonstrate God’s knowledge and power despite possible alternative life courses.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, weakness means ‘the weak’ as emphatic verbal noun, ‘one with weakness,’ or sperm as weak origin, a view attributed to Qatāda; initial weakness better fits the next stage.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r3.claim: Strength follows childhood weakness at puberty or when spirit attaches to bodies; weakness and gray hair follow strength with age.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r4.speaker: عاصم وحمزة وعبد الله وأبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r4.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, with readings from ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Rajāʾ, open the ḍād; most use ḍamma. Both are dialect variants.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet corrected fatḥa to ḍamma as his people’s dialect; this did not reject the other transmitted reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r6.speaker: عاصم وأبو عبد الرحمن والجحدري والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r6.claim: Other transmissions from ʿĀṣim use ḍamma throughout or first two forms and fatḥa last; others use ḍamma first and fatḥa later.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r7.claim: Some distinguish bodily weakness with ḍamma from intellectual weakness with fatḥa; al-Ālūsī sees no difference and says either may describe both.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r8.claim: The second weakness refers to the first, while the last is old-age weakness; repetition is indefinite to match strength, despite strained attempts to distinguish repetitions.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p58#3/r9.claim: God creates these stages by creating causes and locations or the states themselves; the direct reading needs no figurative reinterpretation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r5.claim: This fourth resumption returns to signs in creation to establish God's power and make resurrection intelligible, paralleling 30:48; the following reference to the Hour confirms the link.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r6.claim: Allāhu alladhī khalaqakum is the subject with its adjective, while yakhluqu mā yashāʾ is the predicate: God creates what the deniers reject.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r7.claim: Ḍaʿf with ḍamma is the more eloquent Qurashi dialect; fatḥa is also permitted in the Tamimi dialect, and weakness means frailty and softness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r8.speaker: عبد الله ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that he recited ḍaʿf with fatḥa to the Prophet, who recited it back with ḍamma; Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī transmit the report, with no grading stated.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r9.speaker: عاصم، حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p126/r9.claim: The majority read all three occurrences with ḍamma, while ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read them with fatḥa; Ibn ʿĀshūr reconciles this with the report as dialectal allowance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r1.claim: Min is partitive in origin: humans begin in a weak state as embryos and children until maturity, as if weakness were inherent in them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r2.claim: As God first develops people through stages from weakness to strength and back, recreating them after death is no more extraordinary than their first creation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r3.claim: Human development reflects wisdom, a matter of knowledge, while bringing it about in the best form is an effect of power.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r4.claim: The repeated indefinite weakness and strength name the same kinds, not different instances; the rule that repeated indefinites differ applies when indefiniteness denotes an open individual, not a kind.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r5.claim: Adding gray hair signals that no strength follows the final weakness and that death comes next, since gray hair is widely regarded as its herald.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p127/r6.claim: Shaybah is the verbal noun of graying, as in the description of a head bursting into gray hair.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r1.claim: The initial weakness is the starting point of human creation, especially early childhood though it may also include the embryo; strength is maturity, and later weakness is old age, with gray hair clarifying it.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r2.claim: The indefinite words weakness and strength leave their degree unspecified because people differ in their measure.

TABATABAI:30:54-56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:54-56/r3.claim: The successive stages are each acts of creation, not a separate human deity's governance; God is therefore the Creator, All-Knowing and Powerful.

ASAD-NOTES:30:54#n48/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:54#n48/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:54#n48/r1.claim: Although Arabic uses past tense for creation and ordaining, Asad uses present tense to express the recurrent pattern of human life phases.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r1.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r1.claim: After outward signs of divine power, this verse directs attention to evidence within the human self, especially the stages of life.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:54/r2.claim: Reflecting on development from a fertilized egg through strength to aging and death reveals a supreme will governing existence and makes the universe’s eventual end easier to accept; see 22:5 and 23:12–15.

QIRAAT-ER:30:54:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:10#1/r1.claim: This is the same canonical ḍamma variant as word 5, applied consistently across the verse.

QIRAAT-ER:30:54:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:17#1/r1.claim: This repeats the ḍamma reading at words 5 and 10, consistently across the three instances.

QIRAAT-ER:30:54:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:5#1/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr
QIRAAT-ER:30:54:5#1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ḍuʿfin with ḍamma; the source notes a possible subtle semantic register distinction.

STUDYQURAN:30:54/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r1.speaker: Aj, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r1.claim: The initial weakness may refer to humanity’s creation from a base fluid.

STUDYQURAN:30:54/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r2.speaker: Aj, Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r2.claim: Alternatively, the initial weakness may refer to a child’s weakness at the beginning of life.

STUDYQURAN:30:54/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r3.claim: The strength after initial weakness refers to youth and maturity, followed by decline in old age.

STUDYQURAN:30:54/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r4.claim: Quran 22:5 presents all earthly life stages, from conception to old age, as signs of God’s Power.

STUDYQURAN:30:54/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:54/r5.claim: The Quran also speaks of regression in creation and return to the weakest age, when people may know nothing after having had knowledge.

STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r13.claim: A reminder that the Prophet cannot guide those God has not guided is followed by the guilty’s difficulties at Judgment.
